questions.short: What 1.0 promises: outside researcher, theory operationalization, agree-or-disagree rows
questions.question: Three narrowings of the roadmap's 1.0 that only Brian can accept. (a) Should the 1.0 benchmark include an hour of review by an outside qualitative or mixed-methods researcher, or is agreement with the corpus authors' own published coding enough for the 1.0 claim? (b) The roadmap's 1.0 includes theory operationalization (ROADMAP.md:65); Plan #8 keeps within-case causal reasoning (Process Tracing) and moves theory operationalization (Theory Forge, which has no consumer export) to after 1.0. Is that acceptable? (c) The roadmap's G4 1.0 condition names "contradiction disposition" (ROADMAP.md:83). In Plan #8 only one of the author's 39 codes qualifies as a measure of a QC category, and a prevalence cannot confirm or contradict a when-then proposition, so every 1.0 joint-display row says "complements" or "silent: not measured": 1.0 never shows the two strands agreeing or disagreeing, and contradiction disposition is built and exercised only by planted failures. Is a complements-only 1.0 acceptable, or must one row be able to agree or disagree?
questions.blocks: the 1.0 claim's wording, whether S6 waits on a person, and whether S4 must also bring in Theory Forge; whether S2 also measures one proposition's condition and outcome (part c)
questions.resolves_with: A product call about what 1.0 promises: no test settles whether a person's review is required. Prior art: Qualitative Coding set the same bar for its finish (its step 5) and has not met it.
questions.recommendation: Both narrowings: 1.0 claims agreement with the authors' coding and the planted-failure results, and covers within-case causal reasoning only; an outside researcher's hour and theory operationalization are the first post-1.0 steps, so 1.0 waits on neither a person nor a Theory Forge export. (c) Complements only in 1.0: the S1 overlap shows only the author's "open data" code holds a QC category's evidence (share 0.64, next best 0.48, highest two-way overlap 0.18), so a proposition's condition or outcome measured as a second theme would have no human reference, and an unchecked number in the joint display would trade quality for breadth. Measuring a proposition's condition and outcome becomes the first post-1.0 integration step, on a corpus whose authors coded both. Option (c) 'need agree or disagree' costs about $0.19 per S2 pass, worked out: 2 calls x (58,150 input tokens x $0.2168 + 56,700 output tokens, three labels per turn, x $1.4057) per million, plus two definition calls at $0.0043, and its two new labels are checked only by Brian's review, not by an author's coding.
questions.default: The recommendation: the 1.0 claim is limited to agreement with the authors' coding, and theory operationalization comes after 1.0; and (c) 1.0 joint-display rows say only "complements" or "silent", with the narrowing shown on the readiness page.
questions.answer_words: "author coding is enough" / "need a researcher"; and "theory after 1.0" / "theory in 1.0"; and "complements is enough" / "need agree or disagree"

questions.short: Which coded theme S2 measures (the construct)
questions.question: Which theme becomes S2's measurement construct? The quantitative-strand brief leaves the exact construct to Brian (brief :101, ROADMAP.md:349).
questions.blocks: S2's construct (S2 can start on the default)
questions.resolves_with: Brian's call, because the brief reserves it to him; a written rule, fixed from S1's data, gives the default. The measure is one of the author's codes, so the measure and its human reference name the same construct; it is chosen by how much of a QC category's evidence it holds, so it speaks to QC's theory. Her 11 numbered interview-question codes (names beginning with the question's number, such as "1. subdisciplines") say which question a passage answers, not a theme, and are left out and listed. A code qualifies for a QC category when it marks at least half of the interviewee turns QC cites for that category and a one-sided chance test over the 630 turns (hypergeometric) gives below 0.001; the qualifying code with the largest share is taken, and if none qualifies S2 stops and says so. Computed 2026-11-06 over 8 categories x 28 codes (224 pairs): only "open data" qualifies, marking 14 of the 22 turns QC cites for "Conditional and claim-adequate disclosure" (0.64, chance 3e-9) and 14 of 21 for "Labour, governance, priority, credit, and scrutiny negotiation" (0.67, chance 1e-9); the next share is 0.48. "Open data" marks 72 of 630 turns in 23 of 25 interviews. The round-3 two-way (Jaccard) floor of 0.3 is replaced: QC marks only the turns it cites as examples (18-24 per category), so the highest Jaccard among the 224 pairs is 0.18; it is shown on the page but does not gate.
questions.recommendation: Use the written rule: measure the author's "open data" code, the only code that holds at least half of a QC category's cited turns beyond chance. The feasibility readout shows it, both QC categories it qualifies for, the counts, the chance figure and the excluded question codes before any measure is run, and Brian can switch there.
questions.default: S2 measures "open data" and proceeds unless Brian names another of the author's codes; the instrument's definition is drafted from her tuning-interview passages and versioned before held-out scoring.

questions.short: Which propositions the measure speaks to (the S3 join)
questions.question: QC's six propositions are conditional statements ("when X, then Y") that each name two or three categories, and S2 measures one theme's prevalence. Which proposition does the measured number speak to, and what verdict may such a row carry?
questions.blocks: S3's joint display and acceptance A5
questions.resolves_with: A written rule, no test, because a prevalence cannot confirm or contradict a conditional: before any verdict is drafted, each proposition is mapped to the measure only if it names a QC category the measured code qualified for (Q15); otherwise it is "silent: not measured", with the reason. A mapped row matched by prevalence alone may only say "complements"; the number and passage check refuses "converges" or "diverges" on it. The round-3 co-occurrence branch is dropped: S2 labels one theme, and QC's segments carry no category codes, so there is nothing to co-occur with. Rows whose units differ block aggregation and meta-inference, as the brief requires (:143-144). A5 states how many of the six rows are mapped. Measuring a proposition's condition and outcome together, so a row could converge or diverge, narrows what 1.0 promises about integration and is Brian's call (Q12, part c).
questions.evidence: Plan S3 carries the rule (docs/plans/008_finish_workbench.md:227); acceptance A5's expected result states the count of mapped rows and its failure example is a prevalence-only row marked "converges"; QC's theory export has 6 propositions over 8 categories (S1 receipt).

questions.short: Which Process Tracing route S4 reads (the causal export)
questions.question: Process Tracing's answer path is now its draft-audit prototype (its ADR 0004, approved by Brian 2026-11-05, confirmed 2026-11-06), which writes no pt_export_v2; its pipeline, which accepts a QC handoff and writes the gated export, is frozen (Brian, 2026-09-30) and stopped without an answer on its last two hard cases. If Brian names an independent case (Q25), which route gives S4 its causal result? Without such a case no Process Tracing run happens (decision 0017), and this question does not arise.
questions.blocks: S4's conditional Process Tracing run (only if Q25 names a case) and its cost
questions.resolves_with: An argument, no test: Process Tracing's own records settle it. (a) Add, in process_tracing under its rules, an independent-case input to the prototype (the named case's own records, never the study's interviews) and the small export adapter its open question Q20 recommends once a consumer resumes (only fields the merged answer supports, the rest marked absent, never a full V2 claim); the workbench shows the prototype's verdicts in their own panel and the conclusion as 'withheld' while publication_gate is absent. (b) Run the frozen pipeline once on the same proposition as the full provenance reference ADR 0004 keeps it for. (a) is chosen: it is the path Process Tracing scored best and Brian approved, it needs no pt/ work during the freeze, and no 1.0 condition needs a full provenance chain; no committed file carries a publishable Process Tracing gate, so S4 commits two made-up test exports in pt_export_v2's shape with a publication_gate block (one publishable, one blocked), labelled as test data, and shows both in a 'how the gate behaves' panel. The adapter's file declares its own partial schema (provisionally pt_draft_audit_export_v1), read by a second, partial reader. (b) stays available if a reader later needs the full chain.
questions.evidence: Plan S4's conditional route (docs/plans/008_finish_workbench.md:301); cost $0.0555 per run measured (process_tracing efficiency_20261105 README:161-163); Process Tracing ADR 0004 and its Q20.

questions.short: What S4 may test, and on which evidence
questions.question: S4 needs a causal check of a grounded-theory proposition. QC's process-tracing handoff carries no proposition (it exports state.claims; GT_PROPOSITION claims come only from a theoretical model the pinned Open Science state lacks). The round-8 fix wrote a case from the grounded-theory export: one proposition with its supporting interview passages. May S4 test a proposition on the interviews that produced it, and if not, what does S4 build?
questions.blocks: S4's build, acceptance A6, S6's causal step and the causal step of A12's end-to-end run
questions.resolves_with: Reading, no test (round-9 cold review, B1): Brian's decision 0017 (2026-09-25) and QC's own method rule say a process-tracing test of a QC proposition must use case evidence the theory was not built from (decision records, timelines, correspondence for one named case), the six method-selection questions are answered by a person for that case, no automatic theory-to-test step is built, and no end-to-end page may present a same-corpus test as verification. So the round-8 route (a), a case written from the interview passages, is rejected as circular, and route (b), QC adding proposition claims to its handoff, would be the same test. Resolved by prior art: S4 builds the gated handoff, generalising the independent-case input this repository already used for proposition P5 (qc-p5-process-tracing-input/1, which excludes the QC interviews as evidence) and its IndependentCaseSources packet; the causal tab shows the gate, the existing bounded P5 appraisal on PsychosisBank's and TalkBank's own records with its conclusion withheld, and the 'how the gate behaves' panel. A Process Tracing run happens only if Brian names a case with its own records (Q25).
questions.evidence: portfolio decision 0017 (status accepted) :27-35 and :50; qualitative_coding/docs/METHODS_AND_THEORY.md:453-463 ('owner decision, 2026-09-25'); examples/runs/psychosisbank-synthesis-20260923/qc_theory_input.json (allowed_use bounded_independent_case_process_appraisal; excluded: 'The QC interviews are not evidence in this case appraisal.'); src/mixed_methods_workbench/investigation_spine.py:79 and :186.

questions.short: Should 1.0 include a real causal test on a case with its own records
questions.question: Your decision 0017 (2026-09-25) allows a process-tracing test of a grounded-theory proposition only on a named case's own records (decision records, timelines, correspondence), with the six method-selection questions answered by a person, and says the combined demonstration is built only when such a case exists. Neither 1.0 corpus has one. Should 1.0 stop at the gated handoff (the gate shown, the existing bounded P5 appraisal on PsychosisBank's and TalkBank's records with its conclusion withheld, no new causal run), or should finding a real case with both an interview corpus and its own decision record be part of 1.0?
questions.blocks: whether S4 builds the independent-case input and export adapter in Process Tracing and runs it; the causal step of S6 and of A12's end-to-end run
questions.resolves_with: A product call about what 1.0 promises; no test settles it. Prior art: decision 0017's own 'Wrong if' (a reviewer rejects 'two tools plus gated handoff' while a real case existed and was skipped) and its consequence that the synthesis demonstration waits for a real case.
questions.recommendation: Gated handoff is enough for 1.0: it is what your 2026-09-25 decision describes, it keeps the causal tab honest (a test on the study's own interviews would be circular), and it costs no model call. Searching for a case with both an interview corpus and its own decision record is open-ended (the 2026-09-23 PsychosisBank attempt did not find the decision record), so it should not hold the release; if a case turns up later, S4's conditional route runs it, at a measured upper figure of $0.0555 per Process Tracing run (7 calls).
questions.default: The recommendation: 1.0 shows the gate and the bounded P5 appraisal with its conclusion withheld, and runs no new causal test; the readiness page marks the causal condition as changed by this answer, or 'awaiting your answer'.
